name: fit.kailo/kailo
title: Kailo
description: Analyze your own Strava and Garmin running data and author workouts, routes and training plans.

tools.name: context_get_activity_summary
tools.description: Get detailed Strava activity summary including distance, pace, heart rate, elevation, and power data.

tools.name: context_get_activity_streams
tools.description: Get time-series data for a SINGLE activity (heart rate, pace, GPS, elevation, cadence, power). WARNING: Do NOT use for batch analysis across many activities - use dataset_save_activities(include_streams=true) instead, then analyze with compute tools.

tools.name: context_list_activities
tools.description: List all Strava activities with pagination. Browse complete running, cycling, and workout history.

tools.name: context_get_authorized_data
tools.description: Check Strava connection status, plus Apple Health and Wahoo. See every fitness data source linked to Kailo, the channel each arrives on, and which one activity tools default to.

tools.name: context_get_period_summary
tools.description: Get Strava training stats for a time period. Returns total mileage, time, pace averages, and activity breakdown.

tools.name: context_get_marathon_training_benchmarks
tools.description: Call this before creating or evaluating a marathon training plan. Returns observational 16-week percentile curves derived from thousands of privacy-filtered marathon training builds for finishers near a target time. Includes mileage, long runs, and fastest continuous mile/5K/10K/half-marathon/30K segments. p50 is the median; p25-p75 is the middle 50%; p10-p90 is the middle 80%. Fastest-effort completion percentages show how selective each band is. Weekly metrics describe one seven-day week; block-best metrics describe the best value accumulated since the 16-week block began. Treat the data as descriptive evidence, not proof that copying a cohort causes its marathon result.

tools.name: context_get_schema
tools.description: Get available Strava activity types and field values. Discover what activity categories, stream types, and filters are available.

tools.name: context_get_subscription_status
tools.description: Check whether the current user has an active Pro subscription. Pro is required for all dataset_*, compute_*, and sheets_* tools. Use this to debug 'ENTITLEMENT_DENIED' errors or to check entitlement state before suggesting a Pro-only workflow.

tools.name: compute_start_session
tools.description: [Pro] Start an isolated Python kernel. Only pandas, numpy, and pyarrow are pre-installed — for anything else (scipy, sklearn, matplotlib, etc.) pass it in `packages` or call compute_install_package before compute_execute. Session persists variables between code executions within this conversation. Pick a `tier` (small/medium/large/xlarge) sized to the data: default `medium` (8 GiB) handles most single-athlete analyses; drop to `small` (4 GiB) for trivial work; go up to `large` (16 GiB) or `xlarge` (32 GiB) for coaches analyzing many athletes at once or large multi-year datasets. IMPORTANT: Session initialization takes 60-90 seconds. After calling this, WAIT AT LEAST 60 SECONDS before checking status. Do NOT poll more frequently - excessive polling wastes resources.

tools.name: compute_session_status
tools.description: [Pro] Get current compute session status including available variables, installed packages, and session info. IMPORTANT: Wait at least 30 seconds between status checks. Session initialization takes 60-90 seconds total. Do NOT poll excessively.

tools.name: compute_end_session
tools.description: [Pro] Terminate the compute session and cleanup resources. Variables and state will be lost.

tools.name: compute_execute
tools.description: [Pro] Execute Python code for numerical analysis; variables persist between executions. Report findings to the user as text in your response — print tables, summary stats, and key numbers to stdout, then write them up as markdown. matplotlib figures and DataFrame tables are auto-captured and viewable in the web UI at /compute-artifacts/{id}; still summarize them in text since MCP clients can't render them inline. Download saved datasets with the built-in helper: download_dataset('my_runs', 'runs.parquet').

tools.name: compute_get_variable
tools.description: [Pro] Get the value of a variable from the session. Supports different output formats for DataFrames.

tools.name: compute_install_package
tools.description: [Pro] Install a pip package in the session.

tools.name: compute_list_packages
tools.description: [Pro] List all installed packages in the session.

tools.name: compute_list_files
tools.description: [Pro] List files written to the compute session working directory. Any file saved during code execution (plots, CSVs, exports, etc.) appears here. Also accessible via MCP resources/list with URI scheme compute://files/{filename}.

tools.name: compute_read_file
tools.description: [Pro] Read a text file (CSV, JSON, TXT) from the compute session working directory back into your context — e.g. to inspect a CSV you just wrote. Do NOT call this on images, PDFs, or any binary file. The base64 payload streams character-by-character in MCP clients and the user will see garbled output, not a rendered image.

tools.name: dataset_list
tools.description: [Pro] List accessible datasets (your own, shared with you, and public datasets). To load in compute session: download_dataset('name', 'name.parquet'); df = pd.read_parquet('name.parquet'). Save to a bare filename — the file lands in the session working directory.

tools.name: dataset_info
tools.description: [Pro] Get detailed information about a dataset including schema, row count, columns, and usage instructions. Returns a 'usage' field showing exactly how to load the dataset in a compute session.

tools.name: dataset_delete
tools.description: [Pro] Delete a dataset you own. This cannot be undone.

tools.name: dataset_save_activities
tools.description: [Pro] Save Strava activities as Parquet datasets. Use include_streams=true for detailed analysis (hill climbing, pacing, HR zones). Creates two datasets: '{name}' for summaries, '{name}_streams' for time-series data. To load: download_dataset('name', 'name.parquet'); df = pd.read_parquet('name.parquet').

tools.name: context_get_marathon_prediction
tools.description: Get KAILO's marathon time predictions for a date range — computed by Kailo's own versioned model (`model_version` in the response) from the user's synced activity data. `prediction_source` names the connected provider whose DATA feeds the model; it is NOT that provider's own race predictor (Garmin's in-app predictor is a separate number — never attribute these times to the provider). Returns the smoothed midpoint with upper and lower bounds (14-day rolling average). Served only when the user's race prediction source is a provider this interface may serve (e.g. Garmin); otherwise returns an explanatory refusal that says how to switch. History stored before per-row source tagging reads as unverifiable and is refused, not lost — data_recompute_race_predictions regenerates the recent window in servable form.

tools.name: settings_set_race_prediction_source
tools.description: Change which connected provider's activity data feeds Kailo's race prediction model (the predictions themselves are always Kailo's). This is the app-wide race prediction source — it affects predictions in the Kailo app, training plans, and this interface alike — and recent prediction history is recomputed from the new source. Confirm with the user before switching. Only 'strava' and 'garmin' can feed predictions (Apple Health / Wahoo are refused). Setting it to 'garmin' is what makes context_get_marathon_prediction servable through this interface.

tools.name: data_recompute_race_predictions
tools.description: Clear and recompute the user's recent marathon prediction history (up to the last 60 days, clamped to their plan's history window) from their current race prediction source, bypassing every cache. EXPENSIVE and SLOW: predictions in the window are deleted, then re-derived day by day — they are missing or in flux until the job finishes, typically a few minutes. Use ONLY when stored predictions are stale or missing after a data fix or source change; do NOT call it to retry an empty read, and never call it in a loop — while a recompute is running, repeat calls attach to the running job, but a fresh call after completion pays the full cost again. Confirm with the user first.

tools.name: course_push_to_garmin
tools.description: Send one of the user's GetFast courses to their Garmin Connect account. The watch picks it up on the next sync. Requires the user to have linked Garmin with the 'Course Import' permission. Repeat calls with the same course are idempotent — if the route hasn't changed since the last push the call is a no-op; if the name/description has changed Garmin's existing course is updated in place (the garmin_course_id is preserved).

tools.name: course_remove_from_garmin
tools.description: Remove a previously-pushed course from the user's Garmin Connect account. No-op success if the course was never pushed. Does not affect the local GetFast course — only the Garmin Connect record.

tools.name: route_start
tools.description: Start a new route-builder draft. Returns a builder_url the user can open to watch the route render live as you append waypoints. **Always paste the full builder_url into your reply to the user immediately after calling this tool** — it's the only way they can follow along as the route builds, and the next route_add_waypoint won't land on a map they have open if you don't share it. Treat the URL like the most important field in the response: surface it on its own line, not buried in a paragraph. By default, replaces any existing active draft for this user — set discard_existing=false to surface a typed error instead so you can confirm with the user first.

tools.name: route_add_waypoint
tools.description: Append a waypoint to the user's active route-builder draft. The new leg is routed from the previous waypoint via Mapbox using the draft's profile (walking|cycling). Returns the running totals, last-segment distance + elevation gain, and a compact encoded polyline of the full route so far. Use the totals (and the hints block when targets are set) to self-correct between waypoints — distance and elevation gain are both populated as the route builds, so you can decide whether the next leg needs to chase distance, chase climb, or finish out. Elevation values are **estimates** from a sampled per-leg elevation pass; phrase them to the user with that framing (e.g. "estimated 500 ft of climb so far" not "500 ft of climb"). The published Course carries the same per-leg totals at finalize, so the estimate IS what gets saved — but the word "estimate" sets the user's expectation correctly. ``elevation_gain_ft`` may occasionally read ``null`` if the upstream elevation provider hiccups — treat that as a transient miss, not a flat route.

tools.name: route_get_status
tools.description: Return the user's active route-builder draft — profile, current waypoints, totals (distance + elevation gain estimate), and a compact polyline. Use this to confirm progress before calling route_finalize or to recover state after a chat refresh. Elevation gain is the cumulative per-leg estimate from the build pass; phrase it to the user as an estimate. It reads ``null`` only when the upstream provider missed a leg — treat that as a transient miss, not a flat route.

tools.name: route_pop_waypoint
tools.description: Drop the last waypoint from the user's active route draft. Use this when an :add hit a bad path or the user changed their mind about the last leg — no re-routing is needed because each waypoint already carries its own segment polyline. Repeat to walk back further; the previous waypoint becomes the new tail.

tools.name: route_find_places
tools.description: Find POIs of a given category near a point — e.g. coffee shops near the Marina. Returns up to `limit` candidates with name, address, lat/lng, and distance from the search center. Use this to satisfy prompts like 'end at a coffee shop' without name-guessing local businesses; feed the chosen candidate's lat/lng into route_add_waypoint.

tools.name: route_finalize
tools.description: Publish the user's active route draft into an immutable Course. When push_to_garmin=true, the publish is followed by a chained course_push_to_garmin call; chain failures don't roll the publish back, so the response carries both the course_id and (when relevant) the Garmin error so you can explain the half-state to the user. The response also surfaces the published totals (``totals.distance_mi`` and ``totals.elevation_gain_ft``) so you can confirm whether the route hit its targets — this is the canonical place to read the publish-time elevation, which is computed against the full route here even when per-leg elevation was deferred during building.

tools.name: route_fork_from_course
tools.description: Open a finalized course (a published route) for editing by forking it into a fresh route-builder draft owned by the current user. Returns a builder_url — **always paste the full builder_url into your reply to the user immediately** so they can watch and continue editing. The original course is never modified; on re-finalize a NEW course is minted that points back at the original via forked_from_course_id. By default, replaces the user's existing active draft — set discard_existing=false to surface a typed error first so you can confirm with the user.

tools.name: training_plan_create
tools.description: Persist a training plan that YOU have designed into the user's account as a draft. First reason out the full schedule yourself (weeks → days → workouts) for the user's goal, THEN call this once with the whole plan. The server stores it verbatim as a draft for the user to review and activate — it does not re-plan or change your schedule. For a race goal, set goal_text='race' and provide both race_distance_text (e.g. '5k', 'marathon') and race_date_text (ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' or 'in 3 months'); otherwise goal_text='maintenance'. Author interval/tempo days with a structured `workout` (warmup / repeats / cooldown); author easy/long days with the simple distance_text + pace_text descriptor. Days you omit from a week become rest days. Keep paces and distances as human tokens ('8 mi', '7:00/mi') — the server converts them. Returns the new plan_id, a summary, any parse warnings, and a review_url to share with the user.

tools.name: training_plan_get
tools.description: Read a training plan back with its full week-by-week schedule and the markdown context (plan narrative, per-week focus, per-day coaching notes) you authored. Call with a plan_id, or omit it to fetch the user's most recent plan. Use this to confirm what was saved or to reload full context before refining the plan.

tools.name: training_plan_update_workout
tools.description: Re-author a single day in a DRAFT plan you previously created. Identify the day by plan_id, week (1-based) and day (weekday, e.g. 'Thu'). Provide EITHER a structured `workout` (warmup / repeats / cooldown — same shape as in training_plan_create) for an interval/tempo day, OR the simple descriptor (workout_type + distance + pace/duration) for an easy/long day. Omit all workout fields to turn the day into a rest day. Keep paces/distances as human tokens — the server converts them. The week's total volume is recomputed and the plan version is bumped. Returns the changed node and the new week volume.

tools.name: training_plan_add_week
tools.description: Append a week to a DRAFT plan you previously created (or replace an existing week with the same number). Provide plan_id, the 1-based week number, and the list of running/rest days — each day has the same shape as a day in training_plan_create. Days you omit become rest days. Returns the new total week count and the added week's volume.

tools.name: training_plan_activate
tools.description: Make a DRAFT training plan the user's active plan — what their plan page shows, what activities reconcile against, and what can be pushed to their watch. The schedule you authored is kept exactly as-is; the engine does NOT re-plan it. Re-activating an already-active plan is a no-op. A user trains on one plan at a time: if another is already active the call returns another_plan_active with that plan's label — ask the user before retrying with replace=true, which abandons it.

tools.name: workout_create
tools.description: Author a single, standalone structured workout (NOT part of a training plan) and save it to the user's Kailo workout library. Works for run, bike, pool swim, and open-water swim — set the workout's `discipline` (default 'run'; pool swims also take a pool length). Design the workout yourself, then provide it as a structured `workout` (warmup / body of steps and repeat blocks / cooldown). Keep paces, distances, and durations as human tokens ('800m', '5:00/mi', '5k pace', '2min jog') — the server converts them. Optionally pass a `name`, free-text `notes`, and a user-facing `focus` label. Returns the new workout_id, a structure summary, parser confidence + any warnings, and a kailo:// resource handle. Use workout_push_to_garmin afterwards to send it to the watch.

tools.name: workout_get
tools.description: Read one of the user's standalone workouts back with its full structured spec (warmup / body / cooldown, with each step's goal and target) plus a roll-up summary and the resolved focus label. Call with a workout_id, or omit it to fetch the user's most recent workout. Use this to confirm what was saved before sending it to the watch.

tools.name: workout_list
tools.description: List the user's saved standalone workouts (newest first) with each workout's id, name, focus, and total distance. Use this to find a workout_id to read in full or send to the watch.

tools.name: workout_push_to_garmin
tools.description: Send one of the user's standalone Kailo workouts to their Garmin Connect account so it appears on their watch. Optionally schedule it on a date with scheduled_date (YYYY-MM-DD). Requires the user to have linked Garmin with the 'Workout Import' permission — if they haven't, the result is a permission_required error carrying a connect-Garmin remedy. Idempotent: re-pushing an unchanged workout is a no-op; the watch picks the workout up on its next sync (Kailo does not push to the device directly).

tools.name: workout_remove_from_garmin
tools.description: Remove a previously-pushed standalone workout from the user's Garmin Connect account. No-op success if the workout was never pushed (or is already being removed). Does not affect the local Kailo workout — only the Garmin Connect copy. The watch reflects the removal on its next sync.

tools.name: sheets_list_spreadsheets
tools.description: [Pro] List the calling user's registered spreadsheets, cursor paginated. Returns `registration_id`, `google_spreadsheet_id`, cached `title`, and the OCC `version` for unregister.

tools.name: sheets_register_spreadsheet
tools.description: [Pro] Register an existing Google Sheet under the calling user. The spreadsheet must already be accessible to the user's linked Google OAuth credential.

tools.name: sheets_create_spreadsheet
tools.description: [Pro] Create a new Google Sheet (under the calling user's linked Google OAuth) and register it in one call.

tools.name: sheets_unregister_spreadsheet
tools.description: [Pro] Soft-delete the registration (the Google sheet itself is untouched). Pass `expected_version` for OCC — get it from the most recent list/register/get_metadata response.

tools.name: sheets_get_metadata
tools.description: [Pro] Fetch the live spreadsheet metadata (title, locale, tabs). Returns up to `max_tabs` tabs per call; use the opaque `next_cursor` to page through very large tab lists.

tools.name: sheets_read_values
tools.description: [Pro] Read one A1 range. The response is sliced at a row boundary so it fits in `max_cells` total cells; use `next_cursor` to resume reading the rest. Cursors are opaque — replay verbatim, don't parse.

tools.name: sheets_batch_read_values
tools.description: [Pro] Read up to 50 A1 ranges in a single Google call (one rate-limit token total). Truncation is cumulative across ranges; `next_cursor` resumes mid-range if needed.

tools.name: sheets_update_values
tools.description: [Pro] Overwrite a single range with a 2D array of values.

tools.name: sheets_batch_update_values
tools.description: [Pro] Write up to 50 ranges in one Google call. Each item is `{range, values}`; the call is atomic from Google's rate-limit POV (1 token total).

tools.name: sheets_append_values
tools.description: [Pro] Append rows below the table anchored at `range`. Google walks downward to find the first empty row; the anchor doesn't have to be the literal append target.

tools.name: sheets_clear_values
tools.description: [Pro] Clear all values from an A1 range.

tools.name: sheets_add_tab
tools.description: [Pro] Add a new tab to a registered spreadsheet. Returns the Google `sheet_id` you'll need for rename/delete/duplicate.

tools.name: sheets_rename_tab
tools.description: [Pro] Rename a tab. `tab_id` is the numeric `sheet_id` returned by `get_metadata` or any of the tab ops (stable across renames; the visible name is the title).

tools.name: sheets_delete_tab
tools.description: [Pro] Delete a tab. Refused with `cannot_delete_last_tab` if it's the only tab; add a new tab first then retry.

tools.name: sheets_duplicate_tab
tools.description: [Pro] Duplicate `tab_id` to a new tab. Omit `new_title` to let Google name it `Copy of …`.

tools.name: sheets_format_cells
tools.description: [Pro] Style one range: background/text color, bold/italic, alignment, wrap, number format, borders, and/or merge. Set at least one of `format`/`borders`/`merge`.

tools.name: sheets_batch_format
tools.description: [Pro] Apply up to 50 styling ops in one Google call. Each item is `{range, format?, borders?, merge?}` (same fields as `format_cells`); 1 rate-limit token total.

tools.name: sheets_freeze_dimensions
tools.description: [Pro] Freeze the first N rows and/or columns of a tab so they stay visible while scrolling. `tab_id` is the numeric `sheet_id`; pass 0 to unfreeze an axis.

_meta.fit.kailo/longDescription: Analyze your own running and endurance training from Strava and Garmin. Browse activity history, pull time-series streams (heart rate, pace, GPS, elevation, power), aggregate training periods, read sleep, HRV and resting heart rate, get marathon predictions, build routes, and author structured workouts and training plans that push back to your Garmin watch.
